Step 1 no longer uses sim.run --law (M2); steps 2-3 use contact.probe's new model branch (--design with --gap-budget/--samples/--pairs); every sim.run passes --key; the battery and GATE-TRAC-06 rows run in the ADR-GAUNT-01 cargo form with receipt hashes logged, and gate rows are recorded by record_gate from those receipts (they cited the script's log, which no record field holds); negative controls are nc- feature builds run through the control runner's form, NC numbers read from controls.toml; dep N18-CX (seeds CX-169 and CX-183).

The dead-zone negative control named an end-to-end step `dead_zone_mutant` that no script has; it is the step `mutants` of N18a-36 (control `dead-zone-backlash`, the build of BD-084's `mutant-backlash-deadzone`), with its GATE-SINEW-04 registration left to N15a-12.

Added dep BD-093: every referee fixture here (rolling disc, differential base, lip) moves its contact witnesses, which FrankenSim's sustained step refuses without witness migration between calls; a persisting sibling refusal is logged by name and the row goes to `strict` (BD-161), as BD-085 records for KA-389. The lip row had no tolerance or measurement: a 0.1 N·m/s couple ramp, lift-off where the floor normal impulse vanishes, within 1% of W·a, and no lift-off with μ 5% below a/b. The e2e command names its seven fixtures and passes --key (FROB-REF-805 otherwise).

The strict and lockstep carriers of KA-394 were BD-167/BD-168; now BD-161 and BD-167 as N18-KA names them, and the referee run is recorded as BD-085's expressible entry (a refusal is a refusal event, never a skip). The stale-basis control could not fire: r̂ depends on the axle, not on wheel spin, so the sideways fixture (no yaw) cannot catch a world-frozen basis; new fixture `mecanum_turn_sideways` (yaw 90° in place at |w| = 5.50 rad/s for 2 s, then sideways) and unit test `stale_basis_caught`. sim.run commands pass --key.

Admission status was 'a recorded PASS restricted to that tier and profile', but gate records hold status per milestone part, not per tier: each admission row now names gate and part, and a five-step derivation gives not-built / fallback (fired kill row or killed part, KILL-HARDCONTACT on CL-H's lockstep rows only) / pending / failed / admitted (part pass and that tier's row-by-tier results all pass; a GPU tier unmeasured under a passing part stays pending). The example file no longer holds a status key; a hand-written one is a load error. Law check placed after the matrix (222) and before the build check (724), with dep N16a-02 (its admit). The M1 acceptance no longer cites the M2 `--law` run form. The Hessian property test is N18a-15's (10⁵ samples, ≥ −10⁻¹²) rather than a second one at 10⁴. New tests status_derived_from_gates (rewritten), hand_edited_status_rejected, law_check_order, lockstep_row_needs_invariant.

Every sim.run passes --key (FROB-REF-805 otherwise); the BD-080 note records that request as applied. Step 8 asserted the fixed-witness refusal with 'the profile repair first' and kind `FixedWitness`; the envelope carries payload kind `fixed-witness` and N16-REF's order: shorter interval, then --profile strict. Step 7 asserted a literal observed = 22 although the script reads C: now C + 1, the fixture regenerated as tip<C+1>.

Pinned vectors and Random123 vectors recomputed with an independent Philox4x32-10: all agree. The e2e sim.run passes --key (not part of the world address). The helper list now includes N35-24's `by_reset` and `by_engine`.

The first rows left `component`, `owner`, `since` and `status` unstated; now given, with component's closed vocabulary at version 1 (`field-part` on scene-field: low 29 bits of the field-path hash ·8 + j; `channel`; `part`). The collision check also covers the 29-bit field part (BD-200's rule). reset-pose was keyed by joint index, which shifts when legs are reordered or added (against N35-24's rule that reordering changes no draw); now by the joint or body path hash, with the reserved path `world` for BD-195's whole-world pose index.

The six helpers had no way to address engine streams (action sampling, bootstrap, nemesis, …) or reset poses: added `by_engine` (engine-domain rows only; StreamDomainMismatch otherwise) and `by_reset` (keyed by joint path), with tests. e2e sim.run passes --key and telemetry.query uses N24a-36's registered form.

Two-link, free-body, limb-elimination and parabola numbers rechecked.

requests.what: Every `run` and `mutate` verb takes an idempotency key (N32a-09, FROB-REF-805 exit 3), yet about 510 e2e commands across the beads call `frob sim run … --json` without `--key`. Either the shared helper's frob wrapper must supply a deterministic key (script, step, seed) to run/mutate verbs that lack one and log the command as sent, or every script must pass one; state which, so those scripts do not fail with 805.

N18b-29 adds a model branch to contact.probe at M1, the reader that N18a-02, N18a-10 and N18a-11 name for the records they store in the compiled model (§18.4, excluded pairs stay inspectable; none of them can wire it because contact.probe depends on them). Please add to the contact.probe block: inputs `design`, exactly one of `samples`, `pairs`, `gap_budget`, and with `gap_budget` the required `scene` and `pose` and optional `sample`; outputs: the sample list with provenance and rule and `static_max` against tier capacities; the self-collision filter record (tested and excluded pairs, reasons, smallest clearance, filter digest); per-sample gaps in N18a-02's form {g_m, eps_g_m, terms_m{field, fit_a, fit_b, routine, registration}}; misuse is FROB-REF-802; and extend `probe_and_soil_inputs` to check them.

About 96 e2e commands pass `--seed` and 23 pass `--fixture <dir/name>` to `frob sim run` (BD-085, BD-086, FD-FSIM-03, N18a-35 among them), but neither is an input of your sim.run block (design(s), scene, worlds, seconds, tier, profile, law, …). Either add `seed` (the run's root seed in the world address) and `fixture` (a named conformance fixture holding design and scene, exclusive with them), or state the registered form these scripts must use (for example a fixture file as the design argument, as BD-088 does), so the scripts are not refused with FROB-REF-802.

N18b-28 derives the admission of a contact law per (tier, profile) from GATE-TRAC-01's M2 part and the row-by-tier results stored with it, because a gate part has one status for all its tiers. Store those results machine-readably with the part you assemble: per row and per site column of N18b-32 (strict, lockstep-f64, lockstep-f32, cuda, metal) the outcome pass or fail, cited by the receipt hash; a GPU tier that did not run is absent, never pass. The recorder of GATE-TRAC-09 (M5/M6) needs the same.

The reset pose index is drawn 'under the reset-pose stream keyed by the world address'; N35-23 and N35-24 now key reset-pose by the joint or body path hash, with the reserved path `world` for a whole-world pose choice, built by the helper `by_reset(reset-pose, "world", reset_count)`. State that call so two designs at one address keep drawing the same pose index.
